clue.text: Sauciest hint when frolicking making one keen

indicators.note: frolicking letters skip about playfully, so the two words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone eager is prompted by a racy suggestion while larking about.
explanation.definitionFit: Being eager and full of zeal for something is the plain synonym here.

clue.text: Corrupt leader concealing money in shade

indicators.note: concealing means one piece hides another inside it
something corrupt has been spoiled or altered, so the letters of the next word are reworked

explanation.surface: A crooked boss hides cash somewhere in the shadows.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich green is one colour, and a colour can be called a shade.

clue.text: Rum drunk in work produces disquiet

indicators.note: in places the jumbled spirit inside the word for work

parts.note: toil is hard work

indicators.note: drunk means tipsy and reeling, so the letters of rum are jumbled

explanation.surface: Drinking spirits on the job leads to unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Confusion and agitation are what both words describe, as synonyms for unrest.

clue.text: Superior part of bridge, say, showing mastery

parts.note: upper means higher or superior
in the card game bridge, each player holds a hand of thirteen cards; 'say' marks it as one example of a part

explanation.surface: A top player at the card table shows dominance.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the advantage or control over others is an idiom for mastery.

clue.text: Suffer some strain curiously

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone endures an odd sort of stress.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring a loss or penalty upon yourself is to suffer it, a close synonym.

clue.text: One criticising, as it were, prison

definitions.meaning: someone who slams, i.e. attacks harshly in words; 'as it were' flags the made-up word

explanation.surface: A harsh critic, so to speak, ends up behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for jail; also, jokingly, a person who slams or pans something.

clue.text: Doctor is funnily without limits getting hormone

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged
without its limits the word funnily loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A physician is oddly unbounded when obtaining a hormone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person but is a verb, the anagram signal. 'without limits' trims funnily to UNNIL, mixed with IS.
explanation.definitionFit: The pancreas releases this hormone to regulate blood sugar.

clue.text: Sort out legal document over outsiders in error for a director's colleague?

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the earlier pieces above the next

parts.note: to screen candidates is to sort them out
a writ is a formal legal order

indicators.note: outsiders in means take just the outer letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone handles a mistaken legal paper for a film-maker's associate.
explanation.definitionFit: A film director works alongside the person who writes the script; the question mark admits it is one example.

clue.text: Companion rejected mushy food — be less miserable!

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the food word is read backwards

parts.note: puree is food blended to a mush

explanation.surface: A dining partner sends back the baby food and is told to stop sulking.
explanation.definitionFit: An imperative telling someone to brighten up and stop being glum.

clue.text: Traditional group of students in charge

parts.note: a class is a group taught together

explanation.surface: A conventional set of pupils is supervised.
explanation.definitionFit: Something long-established and time-honoured is a synonym for traditional.

clue.text: Role narcotic plays — characteristic of some prisons?

indicators.note: plays suggests the letters frolic around, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Drugs figure in jail life, as the clue suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A US prison is often called a correctional facility, so the adjective is typical of such places.

clue.text: Inspire love in ancient character touring most of ME country in retirement

indicators.note: retirement is a going back, so the built word is read backwards
touring means going round another piece

parts.note: a rune is a letter of an old Germanic alphabet

indicators.note: most of drops the last letter of the country

parts.note: ME is the Middle East, home of Oman

explanation.surface: An old figure charms everyone while touring a Middle Eastern state after retiring.
explanation.definitionFit: To captivate someone or make them fond is the meaning of this verb.

clue.text: Risk missing opening in centre of Jarrow for country activist

indicators.note: in places the trimmed word inside the middle letters of the town
centre of takes the middle pair of letters of the town name
missing opening drops the first letter

parts.note: to gamble is to risk

explanation.surface: Jarrow, a town in north-east England famed for its 1936 protest march, evokes a campaigner.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiker who campaigns for access to the countryside, as the Ramblers' Association does.

clue.text: New car brought round court figure

indicators.note: brought round means turned about, so the car's name is read backwards

parts.note: Lada is a Russian car make

explanation.surface: A fresh vehicle is delivered to a royal attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: Rafael is a Spanish tennis star, a figure on the court.

clue.text: Russian ace possibly I overlooked in confidence

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters may be arranged otherwise
overlooked says this letter is left out of the mix

explanation.surface: A Russian top player, perhaps, ignored me while I stayed self-assured.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-assurance and certainty: both words mean poise or belief in oneself.

clue.text: Smiley not adjusted to show seriousness

indicators.note: adjusted means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grinning face left unaltered still shows gravity.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave formality and earnestness are synonyms of seriousness.

clue.text: Get under way, we're told, with one posing as exemplary figure

indicators.note: we're told signals that the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: to roll is to start moving, as cameras roll
a model poses for artists or photographers

explanation.surface: Someone set off, posing as a paragon.
explanation.definitionFit: A person others look up to and copy is an exemplary figure.

clue.text: Group welcomes eastern sun over house in African country

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the earlier pieces above the next
welcomes means takes in, so the next pieces go inside

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch
S is the abbreviation for sun or Sunday

explanation.surface: A party hosts an easterly sun above a home in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlocked kingdom entirely surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Writer with US actress? It's a mixture

parts.note: the setter calls themselves me
Jessica Lange is an American film actress

explanation.surface: An author teams up with an American film star for a blend.
explanation.definitionFit: A French loanword for a medley or jumble of things.

clue.text: Inexperienced driver stops patrol to make complaint

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so the driver goes inside the patrol

parts.note: a beat is a police officer's patrol route
L is a learner driver, from the L-plate

explanation.surface: A learner pulls over a police patrol to lodge a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: To whine or moan is to protest in a feeble, sheep-like way.

clue.text: Book out principally on sculptor and composer

indicators.note: principally means at the head, taking the first letter

parts.note: Auguste Rodin was a French sculptor

explanation.surface: A volume is mostly out about an artist and a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander was a Russian composer, of Prince Igor fame.

clue.text: Forgetting parking, liking transport

indicators.note: forgetting means leaving out the next piece

parts.note: a penchant is a liking or fondness
P is the map abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Someone forgets where they parked, being fond of vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' looks like vehicles but is the verb meaning to delight.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport someone is to send them into raptures, the same as delighting them.

clue.text: American vessel on lake beset by endless challenge and struggles

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the earlier pieces go inside
endless drops the last letter

parts.note: a test is a challenge
USS prefixes the name of a United States Ship

explanation.surface: A US ship on a lake is harassed by a never-ending challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: Scuffles and fights; both plural nouns mean physical struggles.

clue.text: Spire in way oddly in Italian city

indicators.note: oddly means take the first, third, fifth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A steeple stands somewhere in a Tuscan town.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tuscan city famous for its Palio horse race.

clue.text: Farah among friends, skipper touring cricket club in country

parts.note: the runner Mohamed Farah is known as Mo to friends

indicators.note: touring means going round another piece

parts.note: a roo, a kangaroo, skips along
CC is cricket club

explanation.surface: A runner among his pals and a captain visit a cricket club abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skipper' looks like a captain but is a jumping kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: A North African kingdom, so a country.

clue.text: Body of followers beginning to excite element in Parisian street

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the French street

parts.note: rue is French for street

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter

parts.note: tin is a chemical element

explanation.surface: An exciting element starts in a Paris street with a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage of attendants accompanying an important person.

clue.text: Restaurant area in US state

parts.note: in Britain an Indian is a curry restaurant

explanation.surface: A dining spot's district is somewhere in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A Midwestern state whose capital is Indianapolis.

clue.text: Around end of summer, note a mutiny that's destabilised euro, maybe

indicators.note: around means the mixed letters go round another piece
destabilised means unsettled, so the letters are rearranged
end of takes the final letter

explanation.surface: A summer revolt rocks the single European currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is one example of currency denomination; maybe flags the example.
